ASSESSMENT CRITERIA

The grading rubric

Five technical criteria, ten answer cells. Review the method and performance levels before you check your workbook.

The 10-point technical practice scale is a prototype display choice. Your existing grader produces answer-level correctness flags. Only the ten designated technical answer cells are assessed. Charts, images, reports, and visual judgments are excluded.
LEARNING FROM ERRORS

The mistake library

Common errors in this case, organized by the reasoning to revisit. A matching number suggests a possible method; it cannot prove how you worked.

The taxonomy covers technical answer checks only. No image, chart, or report evaluation is performed.

TRANSPARENT BY DESIGN

How your work is checked

Built from your existing grader

A Python grader running locally through Pyodide adapts the current two-product pipeline in 15 hagit-sales-autograding: the SalesSolution workbook supplies the formulas, and the Python scripts supply answer positions and comparison behavior.

The older 11 hagit-coding-python folder also contains a three-product sales grader and an accounts-receivable grader. Its common-mistake solution template supplies several wrong-answer models for timing and denominators.

The current case has ten assessed cells: B7, B8, B12–B15, B19–B20, and B24–B25.

Inspect the grading contract ↗

Two transparent policies

Concept checks normalize percentages and decimals, accept absolute differences up to $0.05 for currency and 0.00005 for rates, and require full month names.

Original script compatibility reproduces lowercasing and one-decimal rounding from the CSV pipeline. In that pipeline, percentage formatting can affect comparison. This mode is retained for checking compatibility, not recommended as a measure of conceptual understanding.

Empty or misplaced answers earn zero for their designated cells. Formulas without saved results also receive zero until recalculated and saved; their method is labeled unavailable. Invalid formats or required structure fail validation and receive zero for the submission.

Feedback grounded in evidence

Python computes expected results and tests explicit mistake patterns. Only the selected Python findings and your optional explanation enter the local model. The language model receives only the selected criterion, possible diagnoses, approved case policies, and your optional explanation.

The model generates new prose from these facts and your explanation. A separate code-verified check stays visible above it. Responses must preserve the checker status and pass basic format and contradiction checks; these checks cannot verify every accounting claim. AI can make mistakes. The model cannot change scores. Where several methods produce the same number, diagnoses remain tentative.

Only the ten designated technical answer cells are assessed. Visual, report, and judgment assessment are excluded.

No results are sent or stored

Your file is read in browser memory. No workbook, answer, name, ID, feedback, or score is sent to a grading server. Refreshing or clearing the session removes the working results.

The optional model downloads public weights and runtime files from the model host, then generates feedback locally. Only model files are cached by the browser. Hosting and model-download services may retain normal request metadata.

This is a practice tool. Browser results are not authenticated course grades.
